sources.title: MiMo-V2-Omni launch
sources.evidence: Original March 18, 2026 launch names Xiaomi MiMo-V2-Omni. Dedicated image/video/audio encoders feed a shared backbone; it reads text and returns demonstrated text and structured tool calls. OpenClaw executes filesystem, terminal and browser actions. No parameter counts or dense/MoE backbone classification. Reopened October 27: the shared backbone is not identified as a numerically specified Flash/Pro checkpoint, and no total or active count is stated.

sources.title: Model Release changelog
sources.evidence: March 18, 2026 entry explicitly releases mimo-v2-omni with 256K context and text, vision and speech modalities. Adjacent Pro/Flash architecture and parameter figures belong to different models. Fresh full changelog read October 27 confirms the 1T/42B entry is headed mimo-v2-pro; the separate Omni entry contains only context and modality specifications.

sources.title: MiMo-V2-Omni release announcement in API documentation
sources.evidence: Announces public API service for exact Omni, native multimodal perception and agent/tool use. The current June 29 update stamp is not the original release date.

sources.title: Model Deprecation
sources.evidence: Defines system replacement as rerouting to a newer model and deprecation as expiry of the old identifier. Omni was routed to V2.5 on June 1, 2026 and retired June 30, both at 00:00 UTC+8. Therefore later replacement specs do not describe original Omni.

sources.title: XiaomiMiMo public model inventory
sources.evidence: Read all 30 returned public model entries, including Flash, V2.5 and V2.6 releases; no exact V2-Omni checkpoint, config or weight license was listed. This is corroboration of hosted distribution, not a complete proof of nonexistence.

sources.title: Xiaomi MiMo Service Agreement
sources.evidence: Read the actual English/Chinese agreement in its public document chunk linked from the site runtime (s7); direct page HTML is a client shell. July 7, 2026 version covers hosted API service; section 5.1 reserves MiMo model parameters, algorithms, code and architecture rights to Xiaomi.

sources.title: Service Agreement public document content
sources.evidence: Exact document-content chunk mapped to quick-start/terms/user-agreement by the official site. English section 5.1 retains model ownership/IP; section 3 defines restricted service use. Supports descriptive proprietary classification, not an open checkpoint license.

sources.title: MiMo-V2.5 model card
sources.evidence: Fresh original card read October 27: Introduction and LLM Backbone explicitly name MiMo-V2-Flash as V2.5's base architecture, with added vision/audio encoders. Its separate table gives V2.5 310B total/15B activated and V2.5-Pro 1.02T/42B. No V2-Omni size or unchanged Omni lineage is stated; V2.5 is not a size attestation for the retired Omni identifier.

sources.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
sources.evidence: Fresh complete original report checked October 27. Introduction and Table 1 explicitly give V2.6-Flash 310B total/15B active and V2.6-Pro 1.02T/42B. Architecture section describes those successors with visual/audio encoders; full text has no exact V2-Omni entry, numerical comparison or named unchanged Omni backbone.

sources.title: MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Capability Integration in LLM Post-Training
sources.evidence: Fresh complete original paper checked October 27. Section 4.3, Scaling to a 309B-parameter model, explicitly applies to MiMo-V2-Flash. Main small-model experiments concern Qwen3-30B-A3B. Full text has no exact V2-Omni count or named unchanged model relationship; teacher capability transfer does not establish equal parameter counts.

sources.title: OpenClaw v2026.3.23 native Xiaomi provider catalog
sources.evidence: Contemporaneous integration code explicitly configures mimo-v2-omni with reasoning:true and contextWindow:262144 at https://api.xiaomimimo.com/v1. This March version predates June rerouting. It is primary evidence of the integration behavior, not Xiaomi parameter/topology disclosure.

sources.title: MiMo-V2-Omni historical provider record
sources.evidence: Complete indexed exact-model page states March 18 release, 262144-token context and text/audio/image/video input to text output. Direct fetch returned 403 and browser extraction only shell; indexed provider documentation is used for last-documented specifications, not current operation.

sources.title: MiMo-V2-Omni endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Direct JSON retains exact model identity, text+image+audio+video to text modalities, and an empty endpoints array. The public models listing also omits this identifier. This does not establish a currently usable Omni endpoint.

sources.title: MiMo Studio changelog
sources.evidence: March 19, 2026 Studio update adds an Omni experience and multimodal file upload. Platform file handling is distinct from the native input encoders documented at launch; it does not establish PDF as a native model modality.

sources.title: Healer Alpha historical provider listing and MiMo-V2-Omni identity notice
sources.evidence: Complete indexed provider page explicitly identifies Healer Alpha as an early testing version of MiMo-V2-Omni, links the named official launch, and dates release March 11, 2026. Its FAQ states 262144-token context and text/image/audio/video input to text output. This is the public preview milestone, not proof that preview and final weights were identical.

sources.title: Healer Alpha historical uptime page
sources.evidence: Indexed page independently retains the explicit early-testing MiMo-V2-Omni mapping and March 11, 2026 release date. It documents historical availability rather than current functioning service.

sources.title: Healer Alpha endpoint metadata
sources.evidence: Direct JSON returns exact Healer Alpha identity, created=1773260668 (March 11, 2026 UTC), text+image+audio+video to text modalities and no currently listed endpoints. Creation time only corroborates the explicit release statement; it is not used alone as release evidence.

sources.title: P3D-Bench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Parametric 3D Generation and Structural Reasoning, Table 2
sources.publisher: Yikang Yang et al., P3D-Bench research team
sources.evidence: Fresh full original HTML read October 27. Table 2 has Size (total / active), defines a dash as a closed-weight model with undisclosed parameter counts, and gives the exact MiMo v2 Omni row a dash. The distinct MiMo v2.5 Pro row is 1.02T/42B. This later original benchmark supplies no Omni total or active count; it is corroboration, not a Xiaomi disclosure.

sources.title: MiMo-V2.5 original launch and model table
sources.evidence: Fresh full original page read October 27. April 22 launch explicitly reports V2.5 310B total/15B active and names a language backbone inherited from MiMo-V2-Flash with added visual/audio encoders. Its model table contains V2.5-Base and V2.5, not V2-Omni. No unchanged Omni-to-V2.5 lineage is established.

family.note: Normalized family key for the named MiMo series.

release_date.note: Earliest documented public preview: OpenRouter explicitly identifies Healer Alpha as early testing MiMo-V2-Omni and dates its release March 11. Xiaomi original launch/changelog date the named release March 18; Studio integration followed March 19. The mapping comes from the primary provider; accessed Xiaomi launch pages do not name Healer. Preview and final weights are not asserted identical.

open_weights.note: Released as hosted API service; no exact Omni public checkpoint/config/weight license found in the official model inventory. Open sibling checkpoints are separate releases.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model under Xiaomi service terms, not a named downloadable-weight license. Current terms were updated after the original API release.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 review found no supported nominal total for original V2-Omni. Its launch names a shared backbone without identifying a counted base. V2.5 explicitly derives its language architecture from Flash and adds encoders; later 309B/310B/1.02T figures identify other models. P3D-Bench Table 2 explicitly leaves Omni size undisclosed. No named unchanged lineage supports transferring those counts.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh separate review of active/activated counts, later original model tables and named lineage found no Omni active count. P3D-Bench Table 2 leaves the exact Omni total/active cell undisclosed. The 15B/42B figures are explicitly Flash, V2.5 or Pro specifications; no exact Omni expert-routing or unchanged-base evidence supports a nominal inference.

architecture.note: Dedicated modality encoders and a shared backbone are documented, but its Transformer/dense/MoE network class and detailed topology remain unspecified in accessed exact-model evidence. Later siblings do not establish this class.

context_window.note: Xiaomi calls original context 256K; contemporaneous native-Xiaomi OpenClaw integration and exact OpenRouter provider record specify 262144 tokens. This records the original documented interface, not a test of the retired endpoint or replacement model.

modalities.note: Native modalities supported by launch and exact provider metadata. Remove PDF: upload/tool workflows do not establish a native PDF encoder. Tool-generated audio/video demos do not establish native media output.

reasoning.note: Original OpenClaw v2026.3.23 native-Xiaomi integration explicitly enables reasoning for this exact identifier, before replacement. Launch describes multimodal reasoning. This is documented historical interface capability, not a current endpoint test.

tool_call.note: Launch explicitly documents native structured tool calling; execution of external actions belongs to the agent scaffold.

patch.notes: Public preview began March 11, 2026 as Healer Alpha: OpenRouter explicitly identifies it as an early testing version of MiMo-V2-Omni. Xiaomi dates the named release March 18. The preview-to-launch relation does not establish identical weights; capability specifications here describe the named original release. Xiaomi states 256K context; contemporaneous native-Xiaomi integration and OpenRouter document 262144 tokens. Reasoning is documented by the March 23 OpenClaw native integration. Total and active parameters remain undisclosed; no counted base or unchanged lineage is identified for Omni. Later V2.5/Flash/Pro sizes do not establish Omni counts. Dedicated image/video/audio encoders share one backbone, whose network class remains undisclosed. Native inputs exclude PDF; external tools produce any media in agent demos. Xiaomi routed this identifier to V2.5 on June 1, 2026 and retired it June 30 (00:00 UTC+8); original specifications are retained, not replacement specifications.

summary: Audited all fourteen fields for original Omni. Corrected earliest release to the March 11 Healer Alpha public preview through the explicit primary-provider identity notice; preserved March 18 as the named Xiaomi launch. Confirmed original 262144 context, reasoning and structured tool calling. Added proprietary classification, removed native PDF and replaced generic description. October 27 parameter re-audit separately rechecked total and active counts through original launch/changelog, later Xiaomi cards/reports, P3D-Bench Table 2 and explicit lineage searches. Both counts remain undisclosed: the later table marks Omni size undisclosed, and Xiaomi names Flash rather than Omni as the V2.5 backbone. The other twelve assessments are preserved, including undisclosed network class. Recorded June rerouting/retirement without transferring replacement specifications.

parameter_reaudit.outcome: Retain parameters_b=null and active_parameters_b=null, both undisclosed, after fresh separate review.
parameter_reaudit.total_assessment: The exact March launch and full official changelog do not report an Omni size or identify a sized language backbone. Later original P3D-Bench Table 2 explicitly marks the exact Omni row undisclosed. The official V2.5 card/launch and V2.6 report give numerical sizes only for their own named models; MOPD section 4.3 identifies its 309B model as V2-Flash. No supported nominal total was recovered.
parameter_reaudit.active_assessment: Separate active/activated searches and review of later original tables found no exact Omni numerical active convention. P3D-Bench explicitly labels its size column total/active and leaves Omni a dash. Xiaomi's 15B/42B active figures remain attached to Flash/V2.5/Pro, without an Omni bridge. No total-to-active equality, encoder sum or service-ensemble count is inferred.
parameter_reaudit.lineage_assessment: Original Omni has dedicated image/video/audio encoders sharing one unnamed backbone. V2.5 explicitly names Flash architecture and added encoders, not an unchanged Omni checkpoint. V2.6 similarly describes its own models; MOPD capability distillation does not identify Omni weights. API replacement by V2.5 does not establish unchanged model structure or justify backwards transfer.
parameter_reaudit.search_findings: Fresh English/Chinese total, active and backbone searches surfaced official launch/changelog, Xiaomi investor-material snippets, provider directories and P3D-Bench. Full original P3D-Bench and Xiaomi successor sources were inspected. Secondary directories leave counts blank or describe them as undisclosed; they are leads/corroboration only. API request-parameter tables are unrelated to learned model size.
parameter_reaudit.access_limitations: Original launch, changelog, V2.5 launch/card and P3D-Bench were accessed successfully. Complete same-day parent-fetched V2.6/MOPD source PDFs and extracted texts were independently read/searched. The exact API-release URL s3 reopened as an empty client shell; fresh indexed original text corroborated the unified-model description but is not treated as a full negative. Xiaomi investor deck surfaced indexed model descriptions but direct web and HTTP retrieval returned 403, so it is not used as complete negative evidence.
parameter_reaudit.remaining_uncertainty: Neither total nor active has a supported exact-model disclosure or original nominal comparison convention in the checked material. This is a bounded fresh review, not proof that no disclosure exists anywhere.
